# PUMP in the public series, March 2024 – October 2026


*Generated by `scripts/report_pumpfun_public.py` on 2026-10-26 from the DefiLlama responses saved in `data/raw/` (`llama_pump_fees.json`, `llama_pump_revenue.json`, breakdown by product; `llama_lp_*_fees.json` for the other launchpads), accessed Oct 21, 2026. Fees = what traders pay; revenue = what pump.fun keeps; take rate = revenue ÷ fees. Weeks start on Monday (ISO). The last day is 2026-10-20. This is the long view the collector cannot give: the collector measures the crowd position by position for 16 days (`03-sixteen-days-tick-level.md`); these series give 32 months of fees and revenue, but say nothing about who paid them.*

**Three peaks, two collapses (revenue).** First peak Jan 2025 at $149.8M → Jul 2025 $20.1M (-87 %). Second peak Sep 2025 at $55.5M → Jun 2026 $26.6M (-52 %). Third peak Aug 2026 at $58.1M; October 1–20: $46.4M, i.e. ≈ $71.8M at the 20-day pace.

**Revenue bases (annualised).** February–June 2026 average: $398.0M a year. June 2026 trough: $319.4M. Trailing twelve months (Oct 2025 – Sep 2026): $465.0M, against $753.5M for the twelve months before (-38 %). Last 30 days to 2026-10-20: $835.8M run-rate.

**The take rate.** Jan 2025 100 %; Apr 2025 71 %; Jul 2025 58 %; Sep 2025 45 %; Dec 2025 41 %; Mar 2026 44 %; Jun 2026 40 %; Aug 2026 40 %; Sep 2026 32 %; Oct 2026 36 %. The cut from 100 % came in two steps: the creator-reward and PumpSwap liquidity-provider share from spring 2025 (a mix effect: PumpSwap fees are shared with liquidity providers), and Project Ascend in September 2025; since the token launch (July 2025) the rate went from 58 % to 32–36 %.

**Base rate of one-week falls (curve fees, last 40 full weeks):** 7 weeks at −14 % or worse, 2 at −26 % or worse; the worst was the week of 2026-08-31 (-40 %). A one-week drop of the size seen on October 13–19 is therefore not rare; the paper rests on the composition and the same-chain control, not on one week.

Peak week: 2026-09-28 at $17.9M of revenue; last full 7 days to 2026-10-20: $14.0M (-21 %). Largest one-week drop in 2026: 2026-08-31 (-39 %).

**Time to −50 % after each revenue peak week (full weeks only):** peak week 2025-01-20 ($43.4M) → first full week at −50 %: 2025-02-17, 28 days; peak week 2025-09-08 ($16.2M) → first full week at −50 %: 2025-09-22, 14 days; peak week 2026-09-28 ($17.9M) → first full week at −50 %: not yet (last full week 2026-10-12, -20 %).

**Where the crowd's spending stands against the pre-mania base:** curve fees per day 0.97M (Feb–Jun 2026) against 1.91M over the last 7 days (×1.97); all products 2.57M against 5.50M (×2.14). The crowd is still spending about twice the pre-mania base: the thesis is that it reverts, not that it has reverted.

## 4. What these series can and cannot say


They can say how much the crowd paid and how much pump.fun kept, every day since March 2024, and how the product mix moved. They cannot say how many buyers paid it, what each one made, how long they stayed, or whether the operators were the same: that is what the collector measures, and only for the days it ran. The honest join between the two is in `00-README.md`.
